messages:
incident-bot: Pager — SEV2: rapid KV cache growth and latency cliff detected on prod-runtime-5. Alerts: 503 rate up, p95 token latency > 1200ms for /v1/generate, CUDA OOM traces on one host. Auto-escalate to #incidents and on-call.
priya_oncall: ack — I'm on it. gathering context, switching to incident channel. can someone grab the runtime logs + top output for node prod-runtime-5?
linda_sre: i pulled the tail of the runtime logs — spikes in continuous-batching commit 2026-03-12 (batch-policy v2) right before the cliff. KV cache allocations show repeated growth with fragmentation warnings. attaching quick snippets:
```
[2026-03-15T03:21:12Z] kv_cache: allocate 64MB slab id=42
[2026-03-15T03:21:12Z] kv_cache: free 0 bytes, frag=0.78
[2026-03-15T03:21:13Z] runtime: batch size 512 -> 2048 (auto-burst)
[2026-03-15T03:21:13Z] cuda: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
```
priya_oncall: thanks linda. tom, any known breaking changes in the allocator or batch autoscaler?
tom_runtime: not in allocator itself — last change was the batch autoscaler heuristics (v2) that upsizes aggressively under queued tokens. I suspect continuous-batching + aggressive upsize == many large ephemeral batches pinned in KV slots, leading to fragmentation and cudaMalloc churn. quick mitigation: disable continuous-batching for the affected model/group or throttle max batch size.
marcos_ml: confirmed — we had a rollout of batch-policy v2 yesterday targeted at throughput. It increases allowed batch size to improve throughput for long-sequence customers. it can overshoot on bursty workloads.
jess_support: customer-facing: we have 3 customers with elevated errors flagged by SRE dashboards (ids cust-429, cust-842, cust-1101). errors started ~03:21 and correlate with heavy gen workloads. they're seeing slow responses and some 503s.
priya_oncall: mitigation plan: 1) apply hotfix to runtime config to cap max batch size and disable continuous-batching on prod-runtime-5; 2) restart affected runtime worker(s) if memory remains high; 3) monitor p95 and CUDA OOMs. who can push the config change?
linda_sre: i can patch the config now. applying patch to runtime-config/prod-runtime-5: set `continuous_batching.enabled=false`, `batch.max_tokens=1024`, `batch.max_items=256`. patch command:
```
curl -X PATCH "https://control-plane.api/configs/prod-runtime-5" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"continuous_batching":false, "batch":{"max_tokens":1024, "max_items":256}}'
```
marcos_ml: recommend also setting `kv_cache.max_slots=100000` temporarily to limit growth while we investigate.
priya_oncall: go for it linda. mark the change as a hotfix in the rollout notes.
linda_sre: patch applied and confirmed via control-plane, hitting the config endpoint and returning 200. propagating to runtime fleet; targeting node prod-runtime-5 and its replica set.
@sara_infra: i'm watching node metrics — within 30s of applying the patch, p95 dropped from ~1.2s to ~420ms on prod-runtime-5. CUDA OOMs stopped on that host. memory RSS is trending down but fragmentation counters are still elevated.
jess_support: emailing affected customers with a brief status: we applied a mitigation, services are recovering, we will follow up with a post-incident summary.
tom_runtime: good short-term. next: we need to address allocator fragmentation. logs show many small frees and increasing frag ratio. probable cause: allocator arena grazing triggered by large ephemeral KV allocations from big batches. options: enable background compaction on idle, reduce slab size growth policy, and add aggressive coalescing for freed slots.
marcos_ml: also reproducer notes — running load generator against batch-policy v2 with bursty token arrivals reproduces fragmentation in ~10-15 minutes on ci-sim. i'll open a reproducible test and link it to the incident.
priya_oncall: for near-term rollback option: we can roll back batch-policy v2 to v1 for the fleet but that touches many customers. prefer targeted rollback (disable continuous-batching per model or per deployment).
\now linda_sre: performing rolling restart of the 2 remaining pods in the replica set to free fragmented GPU memory (graceful drain + restart). will do one at a time.
linda_sre: first pod restarted, second pod restarted — both came back healthy. observed KV cache reclaim metrics increasing after restart.
sara_infra: p95 across the fleet is back to normal ranges for the next 10 min window. allocation fragmentation ratio still ~0.48 (normal ~0.12) so not fully healed.
tom_runtime: plan for follow-up patch: (A) add arena compaction pass triggered when fragmentation > 0.35 and GPU idle > 200ms, (B) throttle batch autoscaler growth rate to avoid >2x jump in single scaling event, (C) add guard `cudaMalloc` retry backoff to reduce churn. I'll create the runtime PR and tag for priority.
marcos_ml: i'll push the test to reproduce allocator churn into the perf-suite and add it to nightly runs — want to catch regressions before rollout.
priya_oncall: customer impact summary for SRE/pgm: - duration: ~03:21 — 03:40 (19m) from alert to stabilized - severity: SEV2 (degraded responses, limited 503s) - customers impacted: 3 high-throughput tenants (cust-429 highest; they saw 17% error rate at peak) - mitigation: config hotfix + rolling restarts - action items: follow-up allocator patch, extended canary for batch-policy v2, add regression test, communication to affected customers.
jess_support: creating incident slack thread in #product-ops with summary and next steps, also adding to status page.
own_next: i'm taking next on-call shift in 5m. priya, anything to hand off?
priya_oncall: handing off. runbook: if errors reappear, first action is to toggle continuous-batching off for the model group, then cap batch sizes, and escalate to tom for runtime-level patch. linked PR: none yet; follow-up ticket: INF-7861 (allocator compaction).
own_next: ack — will watch the next 2 hours and keep paging if anything regresses. :thumbsup:
marcos_ml: postmortem owner: me + tom; i'll open a postmortem doc and include perf reproducer, timeline, root cause hypothesis, and customer impact.
priya_oncall: marking incident as mitigated, leaving as postmortem required. closing the pager for now but leaving thread open for follow-ups. thanks everyone. :heart:
